plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 5-date timeline completes: 3 Oct 1819 (Goethe hands 25-year-old Friedlieb Ferdinand Runge a box of Arabian mocha coffee beans in Jena; Runge isolates white caffeine crystals, published 1820) · 1895–1897 (Emil Fischer determines caffeine's 1,3,7-trimethylxanthine purine structure and synthesises it from scratch) · May 1981 (Solomon Snyder, John Daly, and Bertil Fredholm prove coffee-dose caffeine keeps humans awake by blocking A1 and A2A adenosine sleep receptors) · 5 Oct 1984 (James Nathanson in Science proves high-dose leaf/seed caffeine evolved as a natural insect-paralysing pesticide) · 8 Mar 2013–5 Sep 2014 (Geraldine Wright in Science proves low-dose floral nectar caffeine triples honeybee scent memory; coffee genome confirms convergent evolution) alongside the 5-hour human liver half-life clearance curve (200 mg at 4:00 p.m. → 100 mg at 9:00 p.m. → 50 mg at 2:00 a.m.).

teach_overlay.detail: Animated 5-date timeline (3 Oct 1819 → 8 Mar 2013–5 Sep 2014) alongside the 5-hour human liver half-life clearance curve (200 mg at 4:00 p.m. → 100 mg at 9:00 p.m. → 50 mg at 2:00 a.m.)
teach_overlay.scale: because caffeine has a five-hour half-life in the human liver, drinking a double espresso at four in the afternoon is like drinking half an espresso right before you climb into bed at nine o'clock at night
